mainTopic: רוב versus קרוב: the hopping chick, blood in the פרוזדור, רבא's retraction, and cases of found wine tested against רבי חנינא's rule.
overview: The גמרא first explains why the closer dovecote gets a hopping chick: the case is on a narrow vineyard path, so the chick could only have come from those two dovecotes. אביי brings a משנה about blood found in the פרוזדור to show that רוב beats קרוב. רבא at first rejects the proof, saying that case has רוב ומצוי, and backs this up with רבי חייא's ברייתא treating the blood as definitely impure. Then רבא learns three lessons from רבי חייא: רוב beats קרוב, רוב is דאורייתא, and רבי זירא is right that a single majority is enough. The גמרא notes that this contradicts his earlier words and answers that רבא changed his mind. Next comes a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a wine barrel floating in a river. The גמרא shows that both accept רבי חנינא's rule and only argue about how far a river can carry a barrel. Finally, rulings by רבינא and רבא about wine found in vineyards are tested against רבי חנינא's rule. The answer to the last test continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The chick was found on a narrow vineyard path
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the case of the chick is on a path between vineyards. A hopping chick there could only have come from one of the two nearby dovecotes, so going after the closer one makes sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about a path between vineyards. If you say the chick came from somewhere else in the world, that is impossible, because it only hops. A bird that hops keeps hopping only while it can turn and still see its nest. If it can't see its nest, it stops hopping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question: why does the closer שובך get the chick, when we usually follow רוב? It answers that the chick was found on a vineyard path, where it could only have come from these two dovecotes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that most birds in the world come from other places, so רוב should beat קרוב. A chick that only hops stays within sight of its nest. On a narrow vineyard path, that means it must come from one of these two dovecotes. With no outside majority in the picture, closeness is the only thing left to decide between the two.

keyTerms.meaning: Hops; a young bird that cannot yet fly
From the outside world, from somewhere else

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying closeness always beats majority. It sets up a case where the outside majority is not even possible, so there is nothing for רוב to compete with.

phrases.english: With a path between vineyards;
for if it were so that it came from elsewhere in the world,
since it hops, it could not have come here;

phrases.aramaic: דְּכׇל דְּמִידַּדֵּי וַהֲדַר חָזֵי לֵיהּ לְקִינֵּיהּ – מִידַּדֵּי,
phrases.english: for any bird that hops, and turns back and sees its nest, keeps hopping;
and if not, it does not hop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question (on the previous עמוד) about why the משנה follows קרוב instead of רוב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה speaks of a setting where no outside majority exists.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Most birds come from elsewhere, so רוב should decide and the closer dovecote should not win.
steps.terutzMaskana: On a vineyard path, a hopping chick can only come from the two nearby dovecotes, so closeness decides between them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the general rule that רוב beats קרוב, and shows that the משנה's ruling is a special case.

steps.title: אביי's proof from blood found in the פרוזדור
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a משנה: blood found in the פרוזדור is impure, presumed to come from the מקור. This is so even though the עלייה is closer, which shows that majority beats closeness.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learned this in a משנה. Blood found in the פרוזדור is impure even when there is a doubt, because we presume it came from the מקור. And this is so even though there is the עלייה, which is closer!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings support from a משנה in נדה for the rule that we follow רוב over קרוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood in the פרוזדור could come from the מקור, which is the main source and gives נדה impurity. It could also come from the עלייה, which is closer and gives pure blood. The משנה follows the מקור anyway. אביי reads this as proof that the majority source wins over the nearer one.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'corridor,' the passage blood travels through
The uterus, the source of נדה blood (impure)
The 'upper chamber,' a nearby source whose blood is pure
When in doubt, it is impure

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too have learned this in a mishna:
phrases.notes: The משנה he quotes is in נדה.

phrases.english: Blood that is found in the corridor,
its doubt is impure, for its presumption is that it is from the source.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא עֲלִיָּיה, דִּמְקָרְבָא!
phrases.english: And this is so even though there is the upper chamber, which is closer!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the principle behind step 1, that רוב beats קרוב, by bringing a source for it.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that majority (רוב) beats proximity (קרוב).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדה about blood found in the פרוזדור.

steps.title: רבא: that case has both majority and frequency
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. The blood case has both רוב and מצוי, the majority source that is also the usual one. Everyone agrees that combination beats closeness, so it proves nothing about plain רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You are bringing a case of 'majority and frequent'? Where something is both the majority and the frequent case, nobody says otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's proof. The blood case is stronger than a normal majority case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פרוזדור, blood from the מקור is not only greater in amount. It is also what usually passes through there (מצוי). Nobody argues that closeness could beat that double strength. So the case cannot prove that plain רוב beats קרוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Both the majority and the frequent, usual case
There is no one who says otherwise

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying רוב loses to קרוב. He is only saying that this particular proof is too strong a case to teach us about plain רוב.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
You are speaking of majority and frequent?
With majority and frequent, there is no one who disputes it.
phrases.notes: He means no one would say to follow the closer source when the other is both bigger and more common.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: רוֹב וּמָצוּי קָא אָמְרַתְּ
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not the rule that רוב beats קרוב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The blood case has רוב together with מצוי, which is stronger than plain רוב, so it cannot teach about a case of plain majority.

steps.title: רבי חייא treats the blood as definitely impure
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his point with רבי חייא's ברייתא. Blood in the פרוזדור makes one liable for entering the מקדש, and תרומה is burned because of it. This shows the blood is treated as certain, not doubtful.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught: Blood found in the פרוזדור makes one liable for entering the מקדש, and תרומה is burned because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to show how strong the presumption about this blood really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We only punish someone for entering the מקדש, or burn תרומה, when the impurity is definite. So רבי חייא treats this blood as surely from the מקור. That fits רבא's point: this is a case of רוב ומצוי, much stronger than an ordinary majority.

keyTerms.meaning: The priest's portion of produce, which must stay pure
We burn (done only to definitely impure תרומה)
They are liable (to punishment or a קרבן)

steps.whatToRemember: At this point רבא holds that אביי's proof from the פרוזדור fails, because that case has רוב ומצוי. Keep reading: in step 5 רבא learns from רבי חייא that plain רוב beats קרוב, and step 8 explains that he took back his earlier view.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows there are levels of majority. A majority that is also the common, usual case can be treated like certainty, even for punishments and burning תרומה.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches:
Blood that is found in the corridor,
one is liable because of it for entering the Temple,
and we burn teruma because of it.
phrases.notes: We only burn תרומה for definite impurity, so this blood is treated as surely impure.

steps.raayaObject: That the פרוזדור blood case is a strong רוב ומצוי case, treated as certainty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא: liability for entering the מקדש and burning תרומה.

steps.title: רבא learns three lessons from רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי חייא's ברייתא teaches three things: majority beats closeness, majority is a Torah law, and רבי זירא's rule is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: learn three things from רבי חייא. First, when there is a majority on one side and closeness on the other, follow the majority. Second, following the majority is a Torah law. Third, רבי זירא's teaching is correct.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is pulling three practical lessons out of the ברייתא of רבי חייא he just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא treats the blood as surely from the מקור, even though the עלייה is closer, so רוב wins over קרוב. Because the result is severe Torah consequences (liability for entering the מקדש, burning תרומה), the rule of רוב must be דאורייתא. The third lesson is about רבי זירא, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; a conclusion drawn from a source
Majority versus closeness, when they point in different directions
Following the majority is a Torah-level law
There is support for; this view is correct

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Learn three things from Rabbi Chiyya's teaching:
Learn from it that when there is majority and closeness,
follow the majority;
and learn from it that majority is a Torah law;
and learn from it that Rabbi Zeira's teaching is correct:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא – תְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא of רבי חייא brought in step 4 and draws conclusions from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From רבי חייא: רוב beats קרוב, רוב is דאורייתא, and רבי זירא's view is correct.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the contradiction the גמרא will raise, since in step 3 רבא had said the blood case proves nothing about plain רוב.

steps.title: How the woman's case supports רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא said we follow the majority even when the city gates are locked. The woman is like a locked city, and still we follow the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: we follow the majority even if the city gates are locked. The woman is like a city with locked gates, and even so we follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי זירא's rule and shows why רבי חייא's blood case proves him right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With open gates there are two majorities, the shops inside and the meat outside. With locked gates there is only one. The blood can only come from inside the woman's body, so there is just one majority, yet רבי חייא still follows it. That shows a single majority is enough, just as רבי זירא said.

keyTerms.meaning: The city gates are locked, so nothing can come in from outside

phrases.english: For Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדַּלְתוֹת מְדִינָה נְעוּלוֹת.
phrases.english: even though the city gates are locked.
phrases.notes: This is the end of his rule about meat found in a city where most shops are kosher (כתובות 15a). We still follow the majority.

phrases.english: For the woman
is like a city whose gates are locked,
phrases.notes: The blood can only come from inside her body. No outside source can add a second majority.

phrases.english: and even so
we follow the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדַּלְתוֹת מְדִינָה נְעוּלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third lesson from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's rule that a single majority is enough, even without outside support.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's ברייתא about blood in the פרוזדור, where the woman is like a locked city.

steps.title: But רבא said the blood case proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: earlier he said the blood case has רוב ומצוי, so it cannot teach about plain רוב. How can he now learn from it that רוב beats קרוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't רבא the one who said that when there is a majority that is also the usual case, everyone agrees? So how can he now prove the rule of plain majority from this case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3 רבא pushed away אביי's proof because the blood case has both רוב and מצוי, which everyone agrees beats closeness. Now רבא uses that same blood case to prove that plain רוב beats קרוב. Both statements cannot stand together.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it; opens a challenge
A majority that is also the usual, common case
There is no one who says otherwise; everyone agrees

phrases.english: But isn't Rava the one who said:
phrases.notes: This points back to רבא's answer to אביי in step 3.

phrases.english: when there is majority and 'usual,'
there is no one who disagrees!
phrases.notes: Everyone agrees we follow the majority here, so the case proves nothing about plain majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 5 in light of רבא's own words in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim in step 5 that רבי חייא proves רוב beats קרוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא himself said the blood case has רוב ומצוי and so cannot teach about plain רוב.

steps.title: רבא changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא took back his earlier statement about רוב ומצוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא took back that earlier statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying רבא retracted what he said before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier claim, that the blood case works only because of רוב ומצוי, is dropped. רבא's final view is that רבי חייא proves plain רוב is enough to beat קרוב, and that רוב is דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted; he went back on what he said

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final position: רוב beats קרוב, רוב is a Torah law, and one majority is enough (like רבי זירא). His earlier rejection of אביי's proof was taken back.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא holds both views. His statement in step 3 is no longer his opinion.

phrases.english: Rava retracted from that statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one of the two contradicting statements is withdrawn.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא holds the blood case is only רוב ומצוי and teaches nothing about plain רוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא changed his mind and now learns from the blood case that plain רוב beats קרוב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Following the majority is דאורייתא and beats closeness, even when there is only a single majority.

steps.title: A wine barrel floating in a river
steps.stepSummary: רב says a floating wine barrel follows the majority of the town it is found next to. שמואל forbids it even next to a mostly Jewish town, because it may have floated from דקירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a barrel of wine was found floating in a river. רב said: if it was found opposite a town that is mostly Jewish, it is permitted. If it was found opposite a town that is mostly non-Jewish, it is forbidden. שמואל said: even opposite a mostly Jewish town it is forbidden, because we can say it came from דקירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a barrel of wine found floating in a river, whose owner we do not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב looks at the town right next to where the barrel was found and follows the majority there. שמואל says that is not enough, because the barrel may have floated down from דקירא, a far-off place that is mostly non-Jewish. So for שמואל the nearby town does not decide the question.

phrases.english: It was stated:
A barrel that floated in the river,
phrases.notes: It is a barrel of wine. The worry is that it belongs to a non-Jew, which would make the wine forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאת כְּנֶגֶד עִיר שֶׁרוּבָּהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל – מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: If it was found opposite a town that is mostly Jews, it is permitted;
if opposite a town that is mostly non-Jews, it is forbidden.
And Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ נִמְצֵאת כְּנֶגֶד עִיר שֶׁרוּבָּהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל – אֲסִירָא;
phrases.english: Even if it was found opposite a town that is mostly Jews, it is forbidden;
we can say it came from that place, Dekira.
phrases.notes: דקירא is a place name. It is a mostly non-Jewish town farther away along the river.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case connected to the larger sugya about רוב versus קרוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: follow the majority of the town the barrel is found next to. שמואל: forbidden even next to a mostly Jewish town, since it may have come from דקירא.

steps.title: Do they argue about רבי חנינא's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל holds like רבי חנינא (follow the majority even over what is close), and רב does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about רבי חנינא's rule, that one Sage holds of רבי חנינא's rule and one Sage does not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a reason for the מחלוקת: maybe it depends on רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא holds that we follow the majority even when something is found close to a certain place. If so, שמואל follows the wider majority, including far places like דקירא. רב, who follows the nearby town, would then be rejecting רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא tests)
The אמורא whose rule is that רוב beats קרוב

phrases.english: Shall we say they argue about the rule of Rabbi Chanina,
phrases.notes: This is the rule from earlier in the sugya: we follow the majority even over what is close by.

phrases.english: that one Sage holds of Rabbi Chanina's rule,
and one Sage does not hold of Rabbi Chanina's rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the root of the מחלוקת in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רב and שמואל מחלוקת really about whether we accept רבי חנינא's rule?

steps.title: Everyone agrees; they argue about the river
steps.stepSummary: Both agree to רבי חנינא. They argue about the facts: רב says a barrel from far away would have sunk on the way, and שמואל says a strong current could carry it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds of רבי חנינא's rule. Here they argue about this: רב holds that if it really came from דקירא, the bends and still waters of the river would have sunk it. שמואל holds that the strong current of the river carried it and brought it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 10 and shows a different reason for the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is not about רבי חנינא's rule at all. It is about the facts: can a barrel really float all the way from דקירא? רב says no, it would sink in the bends, so it must be from the nearby town. שמואל says yes, a strong current can bring it.

keyTerms.meaning: The bends and still waters of a river
The strong current of the river

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב rejects רבי חנינא here. By this answer, רב follows the nearby town only because he thinks a barrel from far away could not have made it this far.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל both accept that רוב beats קרוב. Their argument is only about how far a river can carry a barrel.

phrases.english: No;

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: everyone holds of Rabbi Chanina's rule,
and here they argue about this:
One Sage (Rav) holds:
if it were true that it came from that place, Dekira,
the bends and still waters would have sunk it.
And one Sage (Shmuel) holds:
the strong current of the river carried it and brought it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the מחלוקת depends on רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מחלוקת can be explained as a factual question about the river, so it does not prove that anyone rejects רבי חנינא.

steps.title: רבינא permits wine found in an ערלה orchard
steps.stepSummary: A jug of wine was found in an orchard of ערלה grapes, and רבינא permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain jug of wine was found in an orchard of ערלה, and רבינא permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about רבינא, which it will use to test רבי חנינא's rule again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine was found right in an ערלה orchard, so we might think it was made from those forbidden grapes. Still, רבינא permitted it. He did not let the closeness of the ערלה orchard decide.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree's first three years, which is forbidden

phrases.english: A certain jug of wine
that was found in an orchard of orla,
Ravina permitted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא חַצְבָּא דְחַמְרָא דְּאִישְׁתְּכַח בְּפַרְדֵּיסָא דְעׇרְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new case to test again whether a ruling depends on רבי חנינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבינא permitted a jug of wine found in an ערלה orchard.

steps.title: Did רבינא rule this way because of רבי חנינא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבינא permitted the wine because he holds like רבי חנינא, that רוב beats קרוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say he permitted it because he holds like רבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבינא's ruling. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will examine this suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most vineyards are not ערלה, even though this jug was found close to an ערלה orchard. If רבינא follows the majority over what is close, that is exactly רבי חנינא's rule. The גמרא is testing whether that really is his reason.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is because
he holds like Rabbi Chanina?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּסָבַר לַהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבינא's ruling in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבינא's permission based on רבי חנינא's rule that we follow the majority over what is close by?

steps.title: Thieves would not hide wine in the same orchard they stole it from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that רבינא relied on רבי חנינא. The wine was hidden in the orchard, and thieves would never hide stolen wine in the very place they stole it from. So it must have come from somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there: if it had been stolen from that orchard, the thieves would not have hidden it inside that same orchard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13. It says רבינא's ruling has nothing to do with רוב versus קרוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 suggested that רבינא permitted the wine because he follows the majority over what is close. Here the גמרא gives a different reason. A thief would not hide stolen goods right where the owner would look, so the jug clearly came from elsewhere and is not ערלה wine.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there (a formula for showing a case is special)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבינא's ruling cannot be used as proof for רבי חנינא's rule, because a separate, practical reason explains it.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" means רבינא's case of the jug found in the ערלה orchard.

phrases.english: for if it had been stolen from it (that orchard),
they would not hide it inside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in Step 13 by giving a different reason for רבינא's ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that רבינא's ruling depends on רבי חנינא; it does not reject רבי חנינא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion ignored that the jug was hidden, which shows it was stolen from somewhere else.

steps.title: This reasoning applies to wine, but not to grapes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the reasoning of Step 14. Thieves would not hide wine in the orchard it came from, but they would hide grapes there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to wine. But grapes, they would hide there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the reason it just gave. The 'thieves would not hide it there' logic works only for wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine in a jug is easy for an owner to recognize, so a thief would not hide it where the owner might find it. Grapes do not stand out like that, so a thief might hide them in the same orchard. That means grapes found there could really be ערלה grapes from that orchard.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only to... (introduces a limit)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think grapes found there are automatically permitted like the wine. The 'thieves wouldn't hide it here' reason does not work for grapes, so they are not permitted on this basis.

phrases.english: And these words apply to wine,
but grapes, they do hide.
phrases.notes: He means thieves might hide grapes right in the same orchard, so grapes found there could be from that orchard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי חַמְרָא, אֲבָל עִינְבֵי מַצְנְעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the reasoning of Step 14 to wine only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idea that thieves do not hide stolen goods where they took them applies to wine, not to grapes.

steps.title: רבא permits wine jugs found among the vines
steps.stepSummary: A new case: wine jugs were found among the vines, and רבא permitted them.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were wine jugs that were found among the vines, and רבא permitted them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new story with a ruling by רבא. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the wine might belong to a non-Jew, which would make it forbidden. רבא was not worried and permitted it. Like the cases before it, this ruling will be checked against רבי חנינא's rule.

phrases.english: Those jugs of wine
that were found among the vines,
רבא permitted them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ זִיקֵי דְחַמְרָא דְּאִשְׁתְּכַחוּ בֵּי קוּפָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new case, parallel to רבינא's case in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine jugs found among the vines are permitted.

steps.title: Does רבא disagree with רבי חנינא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks if רבא's lenient ruling means he does not accept רבי חנינא's rule of following the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבא does not hold like רבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבא's ruling against רבי חנינא's rule. It suggests that רבא might disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא says to follow the majority even over what is close. Here the majority would point toward non-Jews, so following it would forbid the wine. Since רבא permitted it, it looks like he does not follow רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)

phrases.english: Shall we say he does not hold it,
like the view of רבי חנינא?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא לָא סָבַר לַהּ לִדְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's ruling from Step 16 against רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבא's lenient ruling shows that he rejects רבי חנינא's rule.

steps.title: It is different there, because of a majority (answer begins)
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer: רבא's case is different because of a majority. The rest of the answer continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the majority...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to reject the suggestion that רבא disagrees with רבי חנינא. The sentence finishes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'it is different there' tell us רבא's case has a special feature. The word 'majority' hints that רבא may actually be following a majority that points toward permitting. The full explanation comes next.

phrases.english: It is different there, for the majority...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting the suggestion in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבא disagrees with רבי חנינא (the answer is completed on the next עמוד).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the majority in רבא's case points against permitting; the answer begins to show that a majority supports his ruling.
